episodes.title: Superintelligence Needs the Physical World with CEO and Co-Founder of Arda Bob McGrew
episodes.about: Is the AI singularity actually coming? Bob McGrew, former Chief Research Officer at OpenAI, argues that superintelligence won’t arrive without changes in the physical world, and that the “hard takeoff” argument is wrong. Sarah Guo and Elad Gil sit down with Bob, an early key executive at Palantir who later led research at OpenAI. He is now CEO and co-founder of Arda, which is leveraging AI to make American manufacturing competitive. Bob explains why automating AI researchers is a one-time boost rather than a runaway loop, and why GPUs, compute, wet labs, and factories are the real bottlenecks. They cover Arda’s work with Anduril on everything from actuators to missiles to the Fury combat aircraft, why Arda is building “Cursor for manufacturing engineers”, and how the forward deployed engineering model really works.
episodes.why: Bob McGrew, who ran research at OpenAI, argues the hard takeoff is wrong: automating AI researchers is a one-time boost, and the real bottlenecks are GPUs, wet labs and factories, so superintelligence has to wait on the physical world.

episodes.title: The 10 Biggest Days in AI History
episodes.about: On the day of Anthropic’s IPO, NLW looks back at the 10 days that shaped generative AI. From OpenAI’s founding and the launch of ChatGPT to the DeepSeek selloff and Claude’s coding breakthrough, each changed what AI could do, who was ahead, or who got a say in what happened next.
episodes.why: On Anthropic's IPO day, NLW ranks the 10 days that shaped generative AI — OpenAI's founding, ChatGPT's launch, the DeepSeek selloff, Claude's coding breakthrough — by what each changed about capability, who was ahead, and who got a say.

episodes.title: Pika Enact: Can You Direct AI Video While It Plays?
episodes.about: What if making an AI video felt less like writing a prompt and more like directing a film set? Pika is experimenting with a new approach called Enact: interactive AI-generated scenes where a creator can drag an actor into position, speak to the performers, or rethink a camera move while the scene is taking shape. Instead of asking for another finished clip, the director participates in the process. Pika CEO and co-founder Demi Guo joins creative leaders Matan Cohen-Grumi and Lindsay Brillson to explain the idea behind Enact, why these tools feel different from conventional AI video generators, and what their team had to invent to make responsive generation work. We also get into the limitations: video quality versus speed, what an AI actor needs to remember from a director, camera control, access to Pika's H3 Flex model, and who owns creative work made with AI.
episodes.why: Pika's Enact lets a director drag an actor into position, talk to the performers and rethink a camera move while an AI scene is still generating, instead of prompting for another finished clip; CEO Demi Guo explains what had to be invented to make it respond live.

episodes.title: AI guardrails, data center demands, and the fight for jobs | Reid Hoffman
episodes.about: In a special live Reid Riffs from Masters of Scale Summit, Reid Hoffman and Aria Finger tackle rapid-fire questions in a new segment called “Pardon the Disruption.” Reid digs into steering the AI frontier rather than slowing it, negotiating data center deals that benefit towns, and earning public trust amid AI job disruption. Manas AI co-founder Ujjwal Singh joins to explain how AI shrinks early drug discovery from years to weeks.
episodes.why: Discovery pick — Possible is Reid Hoffman's show about what new technology makes possible, not an AI show; in a live summit riff he takes rapid-fire questions on steering the frontier instead of slowing it, data-center deals that benefit towns, and earning trust amid job disruption, plus Manas AI on shrinking drug discovery from years to weeks.

episodes.title: Nvidia Faces Its Future Without Jensen Huang
episodes.about: This week Jason Howell and Jeff Jarvis examine Jensen Huang’s bid to return to Nvidia, the board’s refusal, and the questions facing the company after another enormous quarter. They discuss Anthropic’s approaching IPO, Alibaba’s closed Qwen4-Max release, California’s lawsuit over OpenAI’s escaped agents, and Google’s warning about automated cyberattacks. Also in this episode, Jason demonstrates his Even G2 smart glasses and explains why keeping his AI instructions on his own hard drive makes switching tools easier. The speed round covers GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol, Claude Whiteboards, Sheets and Data, Android XR glasses, and the Apple Watch’s conversation summaries.
episodes.why: Discovery pick — AI Inside is a weekly AI news show from Jason Howell and Jeff Jarvis, new to this list; this week covers Alibaba's closed Qwen4-Max, California's lawsuit over OpenAI's escaped agents, Google's warning on automated cyberattacks, and Huang's failed bid to return, plus a hands-on with the Even G2 smart glasses.
